newsitem.title: USA: Arris is an appealing play - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Arris is an appealing play - Barron's.

text.p: Arris Pharmaceutical Corp, which went public in November 1993 and earlier this year sold a block of chares to fortify its treasury, is an appealing biotech company, Alan Abelson stated in his Up & Down Wall Street column in the September 23 issue of Barron's.
He notes that what he finds especially appealing about Arris "is that it so manifestly falls into the category of promise rather than promotion."
Abelson said the company has intriguing potential products and partnerships with big firms such as Bayer, Pharmacia & Upjohn,and SmithKline Beecham.
Of particular interest is Arris's lead drug APC 366-A, being developed with Bayer, for the treatment of asthma.
The article points out that the firm's stock has been languishing over the past year, ranging between $9-1/4 and $19-1/2. Arris closed at $12 on Friday on the Nasdaq National Market System.
"Yet with its asthma drug and the Bayer connection, it has a drug in the late stages of a partner's pipeline and hence would seem ripe for rediscovery," said Abelson.
